title: Degree-one derived classes classify short exact extensions
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian] with derived category $D(\mathcal A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and let $P,Q\in\mathcal A$. Sending a short exact sequence $0\to P\xrightarrow{u}B\xrightarrow{v}Q\to0$ [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence] to its connecting morphism $Q[0]\to P[0][1]$ is a bijection from isomorphism classes of such sequences to $\operatorname{Ext}^1_{\mathcal A}(Q,P)$ [def-pc-ext]. Here two sequences are isomorphic precisely when there is an isomorphism $h:B\to B'$ satisfying $h\circ u=u'$ and $v'\circ h=v$, so that the endpoint maps are identities. For any exact additive functor $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ to another abelian category with derived category, the class of the image short exact sequence is the image of its class under the termwise derived functor $D(F)$.

source.place: Tag 06XV, lemma-ext-1; Tag 06XU, lemma-yoneda-extension, with degree-one equivalence of extensions. Exact-functor compatibility follows by applying the termwise exact functor to the single-complex triangle; Mathlib Ext.mapExactFunctor_extClass covers this compatibility alone.

proof.text: Put $S(A)=A[0]$ and let $\mathcal H$ be the standard heart in $D(\mathcal A)$. By [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category], its objects have cohomology only in degree zero. The objects $S(A)$ belong to it by direct computation of single-complex cohomology. By [lem-sf-derived-concentrated-single] every object of $\mathcal H$ is isomorphic to some $S(A)$. The Hom maps are bijective by [lem-weil-pbc-derived-single-fully-faithful]. Thus $S:\mathcal A\to\mathcal H$ is an additive equivalence. It preserves and reflects short exact sequences: the kernel and cokernel universal properties transfer along these Hom bijections and the essential surjectivity. We may consequently use the heart short-exact-sequence criterion on sequences from $\mathcal A$.

source.place: Example 1.2.1; Example 1.3.2(i); standard heart identification; also Stacks 06XS(2)

proof.text: For a short exact sequence $E=(0\to P\xrightarrow uB\xrightarrow vQ\to0)$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle] to the corresponding degreewise short exact sequence of single complexes. It gives a distinguished triangle $S(P)\xrightarrow{S(u)}S(B)\xrightarrow{S(v)}S(Q)\xrightarrow{\delta_E}S(P)[1]$. By [def-pc-ext] its last arrow is an element of $\operatorname{Ext}^1_{\mathcal A}(Q,P)$. For an endpoint-identity isomorphism of extensions the naturality equation of the same node is $\mathrm{id}_{S(P)[1]}\delta_E=\delta_{E'}\mathrm{id}_{S(Q)}$. Hence the assignment descends to the stated isomorphism classes.

Let $\xi:S(Q)\to S(P)[1]$. TR1 and inverse rotation (TR2) of [def-weil-triangulated-category] give a distinguished triangle $S(P)\to M\to S(Q)\xrightarrow{\xi}S(P)[1]$. More explicitly, complete $\xi$ to $S(Q)\xrightarrow{\xi}S(P)[1]\xrightarrow aC\xrightarrow bS(Q)[1]$. Two inverse rotations give $S(P)\xrightarrow{-a[-1]}C[-1]\xrightarrow{-b[-1]}S(Q)\xrightarrow{\xi}S(P)[1]$, so take $M=C[-1]$; its last arrow is exactly $\xi$. Both endpoints lie in the standard heart, so its extension closure, clause (2) of [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles], puts $M$ in that heart. Step 1 identifies $M$ with $S(B)$, and fullness lifts the first two arrows to $u:P\to B$ and $v:B\to Q$. Clause (4) of the heart lemma makes this a short exact sequence in the heart, hence in $\mathcal A$ by step 1. Its canonical boundary from step 2 equals $\xi$ by the uniqueness assertion in clause (4). This proves surjectivity without assuming enough injectives or projectives.

source.place: Sections 1.2.3, 1.3.4 and 1.3.6; Stacks 0145 TR1-TR2; triangulated proof of the conclusion of 06XV

proof.text: Suppose $\delta_E=\delta_{E'}$. Rotate the two triangles of step 2 twice, so their first arrows are the common map $S(Q)\xrightarrow{\delta_E}S(P)[1]$. TR3 of [def-weil-triangulated-category], with identity maps on these two vertices, completes to a morphism of these rotated triangles. By [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso] its remaining component $S(B)[1]\to S(B')[1]$ is an isomorphism. Writing this component as $t$, the rotated arrows are $-S(u)[1]$ and $-S(v)[1]$. The triangle squares are $t\circ(-S(u)[1])=-S(u\prime)[1]$ and $(-S(v\prime)[1])\circ t=-S(v)[1]$. Cancelling minus signs and applying $[-1]$ yields $b:S(B)\xrightarrow{\sim}S(B')$ with $bS(u)=S(u')$ and $S(v')b=S(v)$. Fullness in [lem-weil-pbc-derived-single-fully-faithful] lifts $b$ and $b^{-1}$ to $h$ and $k$ in $\mathcal A$; faithfulness applied to their composites gives $kh=\mathrm{id}$ and $hk=\mathrm{id}$, and applied to the squares gives $hu=u'$ and $v'h=v$. This is exactly an endpoint-identity isomorphism of extensions, proving injectivity.

source.place: Tag 0145 TR2-TR3; Tag 014A, lemma-third-isomorphism-triangle; triangulated proof of the conclusion of 06XV

proof.text: The boundary in step 2 and the canonical cone boundary used by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-ses-triangle-image] both complete the same two maps to distinguished triangles. All three terms belong to the standard heart, so clause (4) of [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles] identifies these boundaries. For an exact additive $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$, use [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-ses-triangle-image] on $E$. With its single-complex comparisons $\varphi_A:D(F)(A[0])\xrightarrow{\sim}F(A)[0]$ and shift comparison $c$, it states $\varphi_P[1]\circ c_{P[0]}\circ D(F)(\delta_E)=\delta_{F(E)}\circ\varphi_Q$. Equivalently $\delta_{F(E)}=\varphi_P[1]\circ c_{P[0]}\circ D(F)(\delta_E)\circ\varphi_Q^{-1}$, which is precisely the image of the derived Hom class under $D(F)$. Exactness supplies the image short exact sequence; the displayed equation proves the required compatibility, with both endpoint and shift comparisons explicit.
